metadata.title: Are 15-year-olds prepared to deal with fake news and misinformation?

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA in Focus synthesis uses PISA 2018 results and reports OECD-average percentages and index relationships derived from the PISA 2018 database tables referenced in the text (e.g., Table B.2.6, B.5.11, B.5.12c, B.2.8). The document does not specify whether analysts applied student/sampling weights or replicate weights in the computations shown, so the exact weighting variable names and variance estimation approach are not recoverable from the excerpt. For PISA analyses, users should apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate-weight procedures when estimating standard errors and confidence intervals, and they should use the PISA scaling/estimation conventions for indices and item-based proficiency measures. Because this is a secondary OECD publication rather than a re-estimation study, the weighting details are best taken from the underlying PISA 2018 technical documentation and the cited database tables.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This publication is a descriptive policy brief that reports PISA 2018 percentages, index values, and associations (e.g., R²) using OECD database tables, but it does not present an original student-level predictive model with an explicit plausible-values (PV) estimation procedure. As a result, PV handling and missing-data procedures are not documented in the text provided; the computations are assumed to follow the PISA 2018 database/table production standards rather than being re-implemented here. Therefore, missing-data handling is treated as not reported for this specific OECD in Focus document.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 student data as published in the OECD PISA 2018 database tables referenced throughout the brief. The document does not report a custom analytic subsample selection (e.g., grade restriction beyond the standard PISA target age of 15-year-olds, or exclusions beyond those already applied in the cited database tables). For the Spain comparability note, the brief flags that some Spanish regions administered high-stakes exams earlier, potentially affecting engagement, but it does not describe a re-filtering rule for the analysis shown.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA in Focus brief synthesises PISA 2018 evidence on whether 15-year-olds are prepared to deal with fake news and misinformation through in-school opportunities to learn digital reading and credibility skills. It reports that, on average across OECD countries, 54% of students were taught how to recognise whether information is subjective or biased, with large cross-country variation (e.g., over 70% in Australia, Canada, Denmark and the United States; under 45% in Israel, Latvia, the Slovak Republic, Slovenia and Switzerland). The brief also shows socio-economic gradients: students from advantaged backgrounds score higher on an index of knowledge of reading strategies for assessing source credibility, and about one-third (32%) of the reading-performance gap is indirectly associated with differences in this knowledge. Finally, it reports a strong association between opportunity to learn biased-information detection and performance on a PISA reading item distinguishing fact from opinion (R²=0.46 across OECD countries; weaker R²=0.15 across all participating countries), even after accounting for per-capita GDP or reading performance. The document is descriptive and does not re-estimate models with explicit PV or missing-data procedures, so causal interpretation is limited.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a PISA in Focus policy brief that reports descriptive statistics and associations from the PISA 2018 database tables rather than conducting an original ML modelling exercise. Consequently, there is no student-level ML algorithm, no explicit PV estimation strategy, and no reported analytic sample size or per-country N in the provided text. The extraction therefore leaves total_students and per-country n_students as null and uses framework-appropriate defaults for PV and missing-data handling.
